descriptors: All learning objectives and state content standards*, and their connection to student work expectations, are explicitly communicated and understood by students.

The lesson starts promptly.
The lesson’s structure is coherent, based on the content, and organized to meet students’ needs, with time for reflection to ensure student understanding.
Pacing is brisk, adjusted for rigor of content and individual student learning expectations.
Students’ individual needs are attended to and pacing provides many opportunities for individual students who progress at different learning rates.
Students understand and engage in classroom routines and transitions to ensure efficient use of time.

Activities and materials include all of the following Content aspects: support the lesson objectives; are challenging; elicit a variety of thinking; provide time for reflection; and are relevant to students’ lives.

Activities and materials include all of the following Student-centered aspects: sustain students’ attention; provide opportunities for student-to-student interaction; evoke student curiosity and suspense; and provide students with choices when appropriate and aligned to the learning objectives.

Activities and materials include all of the following Multiple materials aspects: incorporate additional standards-based resources where appropriate to support individual and whole group understanding (e.g., visuals, multimedia, technology, manipulatives, resources from museums, cultural centers, etc., when not available in the high-quality instructional materials).

In addition, sometimes activities are game-like, involve simulations, require creating products, and demand self-direction, and students are continuously self-monitoring as appropriate to enhance learning.

Activities and materials include a majority of the following Content aspects: support the lesson objectives; are challenging; elicit a variety of thinking; provide time for reflection; and are relevant to students’ lives.

Activities and materials include a majority of the following Student-centered aspects: sustain students’ attention; provide opportunities for student-to-student interaction; evoke student curiosity and suspense; and provide students with choices when appropriate and aligned to the learning objectives.

Activities and materials include a majority of the following Multiple materials aspects: incorporate additional standards-based resources where appropriate to support individual and whole group understanding (e.g., visuals, multimedia, technology, manipulatives, resources from museums, cultural centers, etc., when not available in the high-quality instructional materials).

Activities and materials include a few of the following Content aspects: support the lesson objectives; are challenging; elicit a variety of thinking; provide time for reflection; or are relevant to students’ lives.

Activities and materials include a few of the following Student-centered aspects: sustain students’ attention; provide opportunities for student-to-student interaction; evoke student curiosity and suspense; or provide students with choices.

Activities and materials include a few of the following Multiple materials aspects: incorporate additional standards-based resources where appropriate to support individual and whole group understanding (e.g., visuals, multimedia, technology, manipulatives, resources from museums, cultural centers, etc., when not available in the high-quality instructional materials).

Students are actively engaged in multiple types of thinking: analytical thinking, where students analyze, compare and contrast, and evaluate and explain information; practical thinking, where students use, apply, and implement what they learn in real-life scenarios; creative thinking, where students create, design, imagine, and suppose; and research-based thinking, where students explore and review a variety of ideas, models, and solutions to problems.

Instructional plans include: evidence of the internalization of the plans from the high-quality curriculum;
Instructional plans include: measurable and explicit objectives aligned to state standards and aligned high-quality curriculum, both in content and in rigor;

Instructional plans include: activities, materials, and assessments that: are aligned to state standards, content, including high-quality curriculum, and success criteria; are sequenced and scaffolded based on student need; build on prior student knowledge, are relevant to students’ lives, and integrate other disciplines as appropriate; and provide appropriate time for student work, student reflection, and lesson closure;
Instructional plans include: evidence that the plan is appropriate for the age, knowledge, and interests of all learners;
Instructional plans include: evidence that the plan provides regular opportunities to accommodate individual student needs; and
